title: Error Handling
concept: Handle async/await errors with try/catch and Promise errors with .catch()

steps.title: Promise Rejection at await
steps.explanation:
`await` calls `riskyOperation()`.
This function throws an error, so the returned Promise becomes 'rejected'.
`await` treats this rejected Promise like a regular `throw` statement.
steps.keyInsight: rejected Promise at await = same as throw

steps.title: catch Block Executes
steps.explanation:
The error thrown by `await` is caught by the nearest `catch` block.
The rest of the `try` block (line 9) is skipped.

steps.title: Print the Error Message
steps.explanation:
The `catch` block executes and prints the error object's message to the console.
The program continues without crashing.

steps.title: Alternative: .catch() Chaining
steps.explanation:
This code doesn't actually run here, but it shows another way to handle Promise errors without `async/await`.
Attaching `.catch()` at the end of a chain catches rejections from anywhere in that chain.
steps.keyInsight: async/await with try/catch is syntactic sugar for Promise with .catch().

options: The callback runs after try/catch has already finished
quiz.explanation:
try/catch only catches synchronous code.
The setTimeout callback runs from the Task Queue after try/catch has already finished, so it can't be caught.

misconceptions.correct:
try/catch only catches synchronous code and **awaited Promises**.
Floating callback errors are not caught.
misconceptions.why: try/catch catches errors that are on the call stack at the time of execution, but callbacks run later in a separate stack (Queue).

keyTakeaway: async/await → try/catch, Promise → .catch(), callback errors require separate handling
